Bullet 1 names only 'Panta's family' beside Bozz and gives no location for either, so Bozz is the sole target and it keeps a null zone. The Ten of Coins aside is advice for a different quest, and the Treasure Hunter and respawn sub-bullets are strategy.

notes: Three talks in Norg, then three Voidwatch battles, then back to Kieran. The quest does not flag until bullet 3, which is also where the only observable thing in it -- [KI] Ashen stratum abyssite II -- is handed over; the abyssite III of bullet 5 is the header's Reward and so is not used as evidence. Bullet 4's three sub-bullets are three separate battles in three separate zones, so they are three steps and not one: a step has one zone. Nothing in the page orders them, so they share a group and all three draw at once. Each zone lists several planar rift spots and any of them opens the same fight, so the grids stay in the notes and the steps carry none. The zone names already have their articles on this page and all three resolve. 'Zilart Mission 14 - Ark Angels must be started' is a mission gate with no slot in the schema and nothing observable behind it, so it is flagged and gates nothing; Previous keeps the quest that really does precede it. Stage D: every rung, target, zone, group and piece of evidence here survives checking -- the abyssite II is handed over at bullet 3 and used there, the reward abyssite III is correctly not evidence, and the three battles really are three zones -- but 'Zilart Mission 14 - Ark Angels must be started' gates the very first cutscene and the schema has no slot for a mission, so the quest is recorded as gated on nothing and a player without that mission would be marked at Kieran for a cutscene that will not come. An unmodellable gate is a medium by the confidence table, so the quest is demoted; nothing was removed.

notes: The Black Belt quest, and the best door in the batch: everything after the first talk happens at 'Door: Neptune's Spire', which is a real targetable entity -- the resolver folds it to door:neptune's spire -- so eight of the eleven rungs carry a marker where a keyword pass would have produced 'Atori-Tutori', an NPC you never actually stand in front of. The page writes the name in quotation marks; the door's own name has none, and the quoted form does not resolve. Each of the three trophies is split from its trade: obtaining is a separate, observable rung (Wyrm Beard, Behemoth Tongue, Adamantoise Egg all resolve as items and each is evidence exactly once), and the trade is a door step in Lower Jeuno. The alternatives named for each -- Early Bird Catches the Wyrm, Horns of War, The Hills Are Alive -- are battlefields rather than drops, so only the NM is recorded as the mob and the battlefield stays in the note; the evidence covers either route. 'Quest Reqs: Level 71+ Monk' is both gates. 'Tenshodo Fame Level 6' is the real fame gate but the page never names the region that fame belongs to, and its own Fame field says Jeuno with no level, so the header is what is recorded and the Tenshodo requirement is flagged instead of guessed at. The Brown Belt is consumed by the last trade. Stage D: the ladder itself holds up -- the door is the right target throughout, each trophy is evidence exactly once and at the step that obtains it, the Black Belt is correctly kept out of evidence as the Reward, and the bullet order is the page's -- but 'Tenshodo Fame Level 6' is a real gate that cannot be carried: it is not one of the nine fame regions and the header's own Fame field is Jeuno with no level, so the quest emits gated on nothing. An unmodellable gate is a medium by the confidence table, so the quest is demoted; nothing was removed.
